content: Protein odd-skipped-related 1 (OSR1) is a transcription factor encoded by the OSR1 gene in humans. This gene is located on chromosome 2 (2p24.1). In mice, the homologous gene is referred to as Osr1. OSR1 and its closely related transcription factor OSR2 are critical for the normal development of several organs, including the kidneys, heart, and palate. These transcription factors are homologous to the Odd-skipped class transcription factors found in Drosophila, which are encoded by genes such as odd, bowl, sob, and arm. OSR1 is a protein composed of 266 amino acids and contains three C2H2 zinc finger domains. It shares 65% amino acid sequence similarity and 98% zinc finger domain similarity with OSR2. Early Expression In mice, the expression of Osr1 begins during gastrulation on embryological day 7.5 in cells destined to become the intermediate mesoderm. By embryonic day 8.5, Osr1 is expressed in the intermediate mesoderm, lateral to the neural plate. By day 9.5, its expression diminishes and shifts posteriorly to the presumptive kidney region. By day 10.5, Osr1 expression is also observed in the branchial arches and developing limbs. Heart Development Osr1 plays a critical role in the formation of the atrial septum in the heart. It is expressed in the dorsal atrial wall, which gives rise to the primary atrial septum, and later in the septum itself and the left venous valve leaflet. Osr1 is also present in the mesothelium of the thoracic cavity and the parietal pericardium. Embryos lacking Osr1 expression typically die before birth due to severe malformations, including deformed atrioventricular junctions and underdeveloped venous valves. Even embryos that survive to term exhibit an incomplete parietal pericardium. These defects occur despite the presence of other transcription factors essential for atrial septum formation, such as Nkx2-5, Pitx2, and Tbx5. Kidney Development Osr1 is the earliest known marker of the intermediate mesoderm, which gives rise to the kidneys and gonads. While Osr1 expression is not required for the formation of the intermediate mesoderm itself, it is essential for its differentiation into renal and gonadal structures. Osr1 functions upstream of transcription factors such as Lhx1, Pax2, and Wt1, which are critical for early urogenital development. In normal kidney development, the activation of the Pax2-Eya1-Hox11 complex leads to the expression of Six2 and Gdnf, which are necessary for ureteric bud branching and the maintenance of nephron-forming cap mesenchyme. Within the developing kidney, cells expressing Osr1 differentiate into mesangial cells, pericytes, ureteric smooth muscle, and the kidney capsule. The timing of Osr1 expression loss determines the cell fate. For example, cells destined to become part of the vasculature or ureteric epithelium lose Osr1 expression early (around embryonic day 8.5), while those that form nephrons lose expression later (around embryonic day 11.5). In mice lacking Osr1 expression, all three stages of kidney development are disrupted. These mice exhibit abnormalities in the Wolffian duct, reduced mesonephric tubules, and the absence of the kidney-forming metanephros and gonads. By embryonic day 10.5, these embryos fail to develop a ureteric bud, which is necessary for interaction with the metanephric mesenchyme. The absence of inductive signals from the ureteric bud, combined with reduced Pax2 expression, leads to apoptosis and kidney agenesis. Limb Formation During limb development, Osr1 expression is initially localized to the mesenchyme beneath the endoderm. By embryonic day 11.5, its expression shifts anteriorly and proximally. In mice, Osr1 is expressed in the interdigital mesenchyme and presumptive synovial joints, where it overlaps with the expression of Gdf5, an early marker of joint formation. Other Sites of Expression Osr1 is also expressed in the first and second branchial arches, limb buds, mouth, nasal pits, trunk, forebrain, developing somites, distal mandible, and developing eye. Regulation The expression of Osr1 is negatively regulated by the genes Runx2 and Ikzf1. These genes are involved in osteoblast and lymphocyte differentiation, respectively, and interact with the Osr1 promoter region. In human osteoblast and osteosarcoma cell lines, OSR1 expression is directly induced by 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3. Clinical Relevance Reduction of Kidney Size A variant allele of the human OSR1 gene, which does not produce a functional transcript, is found in approximately 6% of Caucasian populations. This variant is associated with an 11.8% reduction in the size of newborn kidneys. OSR1 Methylation in Cancer OSR1 is frequently methylated and downregulated in gastric cancer, with methylation observed in 51.8% of gastric cancer cells and tissues. When expressed normally, OSR1 has anti-proliferative effects, inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in gastric cancer cells. Additionally, OSR1 is methylated in over 85% of squamous cell carcinomas.
